correctness.rationale: The normalized quotient extends continuously to the endpoints. At the critical exponent the published inequality is nonnegative and has the unique interior zero at 1/2; monotonicity in the exponent therefore forces any minimizing sequence toward 1/2 once the balanced-split upper bound tends to zero. Differentiating the balanced quotient gives the displayed coefficient, while a mean-value expansion in the exponent and nonnegativity of the critical quotient give the matching lower bound. Fresh recomputation gives the critical exponent 1.271553303163612, verifies \(2/\rho+1/\rho^2=1\), and gives the constant 3.248289741210747. Finite numerical minimization is only corroborative.

originality.rationale: Ye and Liu prove the critical silver inequality, equality only at 0, 1/2 and 1, and a uniform normalized slack coefficient one in the ideal perturbative estimate. They do not optimize that coefficient or prove localization of minimizers. The audited variational argument turns the isolated equality point into the exact first-order coefficient about 3.24829. The later recursive-composition paper is plausibly related but concerns a different Bellman kernel in the accessible statement; its unavailable full body remains an explicit residual risk rather than a failure shortcut.
